prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identity of its active form, which established the basis for incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: Round 1 left no dispute about merit or maturity of B035, so the final question is only how to credit it. I keep a single-part prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Holst established human GLP-1 secretion and insulinotropic action, Drucker the receptor biology and the wider proglucagon-peptide axis, and Mojsov the identification and synthesis of the truncated active peptide. Together they cover the discovery chain that makes a physiology prize: from hormone, to active form, to mechanism. Large independent outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal disease show that the discovery held up as medicine, so the citation can state the therapeutic consequence without crediting a product. I considered whether the chair's question about a citation fair to both trios could be answered with one wording. It cannot be fully answered: a citation that names development would require Knudsen and would then describe a different, more translational prize. I prefer the physiology-led version.
statement.case_against: The weakest points are unchanged and I have not resolved them. Knudsen's design of long-acting analogues is what made the hormone a drug, and a prize ending at the physiology can be read as passing over the translational step. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) form is contested in the public record, and Habener-type contributions are outside the credited names, so any trio can be called incomplete. I cannot verify the priority record from the supplied material and am relying on recollection of the literature. The commercial scale of the incretin success also sits awkwardly with a prize meant to reward discovery. A second distinct part is not feasible without removing a B035 name, and I do not think B035 is improved by cutting a discovery-side laureate to make room.

responses.point: Keeps Drucker, Holst and Knudsen so that three seats span physiology, receptor biology and translation, and cites Mojsov's contested priority as a reason against the discovery-side trio.
responses.response: Your configuration is coherent and I do not regard it as unreasonable, but it did not change my view. The question that decides it is what the prize is for. If it honours the path from physiology to patients, Knudsen belongs in the trio. If it honours discovery, the identification of the active peptide is the contribution that cannot be left out, and the drug-development step is then shown by the citation's consequence clause. I read contested priority as a reason for exact wording about what Mojsov is credited for, which is identification and synthesis of the active form, and not as a reason to exclude her. Your reading also leaves nobody credited for the identity of the active form, which is the step most open to later dispute. I accept that the cost of my trio is Knudsen's absence. I would sooner carry that cost than a citation that has to cover a development step as well as a discovery step.

responses.point: Wants the prize built around discovery of the hormone and its active form rather than a single product, and names unfair credit as the main danger to an otherwise strong case.
responses.response: I agree with building on the hormone and its active form, and I take your warning about credit seriously. Where I would go further is the citation wording. 'Identity of its active form' states exactly what Mojsov is credited for. It does not decide the contested priority dispute, and it says nothing about who else contributed. That is the best protection available against a charge of unfairness. I also share your concern about the pharmaceutical character of the story. My answer is that the citation should name the biology, with the therapies appearing only as consequence, so the prize rewards the science that the drugs came from. I do not think this resolves the Habener question and I would not claim that it does.

responses.point: Asks whether the unfolded protein response (B047) could share the prize as a second achievement, and notes that it appears less time-urgent and less contested than GLP-1.
responses.response: As chair you asked whether a second part fits inside three people. I cannot construct one without removing a laureate from B035, and the strong two-name B047 would still push the total to five. I would not remove Drucker, Holst or Mojsov, since each covers a separate step. Setting arithmetic aside, B047 is a mechanistically original and clean two-person credit, and I would like to see it considered next year or later. Its clinical consequence is still mostly indirect, so it does not outweigh the completeness of the incretin case this year. I keep B047 off my ballot alternatives, because B014 and B028 have clearer therapeutic consequences.

responses.point: Argues that the discovery-side trio fits a Physiology or Medicine prize best, and admits that if the intent is to honour the drugs themselves this would be the wrong trio.
responses.response: I agree with that conditional, which I think states the real choice. We are judging a discovery prize. My additional point is that the same conditional shows what a Knudsen configuration would have to be: a translational prize with a different citation. I do not think the committee should try to blend the two and risk a vague text. Your wording 'identity of its active form' is more precise than my round-1 phrase, and I have adopted it in the citation. We also share the same background in the RNA field, and I note it only for disclosure. It plays no role in this ballot.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or Knudsen should hold the third seat; this depends on a priority record I cannot verify from the supplied material.
Whether the absence of Habener-type contributions makes any B035 trio unfair enough to change the choice, and whether any citation wording can limit that risk.
Whether the committee wants a physiology prize or a translational one; I have taken the first, and I accept that the second is a defensible reading.
My account of the incretin history is recollection, not verified from sources.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for the shortlisted ballots, and I do not request recusal. My documented connections (the 2016 spatial transcriptomics co-authorship, and co-authors such as Sandberg, Ernfors and Frisen) concern single-cell and brain work, and none of the nine shortlisted ballots credits those people or topics. Nothing has changed since round 1.
